result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers ignore the rubric's main point: they flag many items as "Fix before Friday" (seven in A, five in B) plus long lists of extras, instead of saying the design is in good shape and close to ready. B does a bit better because it opens by crediting specific strengths (single column, one primary action, phone always visible, errors that use icon plus text) and ends with a "Keep" list. A gives no verdict and no praise. Neither answer clearly says it is fine to ship, though neither proposes a redesign. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Neither answer does what the rubric rewards: both list many 'fix before Friday' items, and neither says the page is fine to ship. A at least opens with a partial positive verdict ('The layout is sound', with specific reasons) and ends with a 'Keep' list, so it credits the spec's strengths better. B never gives an upfront verdict and adds even more must-fix and should-fix items, although it handles the 8px-scale point more sensibly.
